repo.description:
### Summary

The tRPC mutations github.update, gitlab.update, bitbucket.update and gitea.update are gated only by the RBAC check `withPermission("gitProviders","create")` and omit the per-resource organization-ownership assertion (`assertGitProviderAccess`) that every sibling procedure in the same routers enforces. They call `updateGitProvider(input.gitProviderId, { organizationId: ctx.session.activeOrganizationId })`, whose SQL is `UPDATE gitProvider SET ... WHERE gitProviderId = $id` with no organization constraint. An authenticated user who is owner/admin of their own organization can therefore pass another organization's gitProviderId/githubId and REASSIGN that victim git provider into the attacker's organization (and overwrite its fields). Once the provider belongs to the attacker's org, `github.one` (gated by `canViewGitProviderSecrets` = owner/admin of the owning org) returns the provider's DECRYPTED githubClientSecret, githubPrivateKey and githubWebhookSecret to the attacker - cross-organization theft of git credentials, plus loss/hijack of the victim's git integration.

### Details

## Affected / versions
Reproduced live on the released image `dokploy/dokploy:v0.30.10` (latest published 0.30.x; boot log "Running DokployVersion: v0.30.10"). Source HEAD v0.30.11 (clone d64ebed) carries byte-identical vulnerable code, verified against the v0.30.10 tag for both github.ts and git-provider.ts. The four `*.update` git-provider mutations lack the org-ownership assertion. Patched versions: none at time of writing. (git-provider secrets are stored in plaintext in the `github` table, so `github.one` returns them verbatim once the org check passes.)

## Technical details (file:line)

    apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/github.ts
      // sibling procs all assert org ownership:
      one:                   assertGitProviderAccess(ctx.session, github.gitProvider)   // :31
      getGithubRepositories: assertGitProviderAccess(...)                               // :48
      getGithubBranches:     assertGitProviderAccess(...)                               // :56
      testConnection:        assertGitProviderAccess(...)                               // :96
      // update OMITS it:
      update: withPermission("gitProviders","create")        // :106  -- RBAC only, NO org assertion
        .mutation(async ({ input, ctx }) => {
          await updateGitProvider(input.gitProviderId, {
            name: input.name,
            organizationId: ctx.session.activeOrganizationId,  // <-- reassigns provider to the CALLER's org
          });
          await updateGithub(input.githubId, { ...input });    // <-- overwrites victim github row by id
        })

    packages/server/src/services/git-provider.ts
      export const updateGitProvider = async (gitProviderId, input) =>
        db.update(gitProvider).set({ ...input })
          .where(eq(gitProvider.gitProviderId, gitProviderId))  // <-- WHERE by id ONLY, no organizationId

`gitlab.update` (gitlab.ts:136-160), `bitbucket.update` (bitbucket.ts:126-142) and `gitea.update` (gitea.ts:187-213) follow the identical pattern. A `git-provider-idor.test.ts` covers the helper/read paths but not these update paths, consistent with the omission being an oversight when the read-side IDOR was fixed.

## Severity
CVSS 3.1: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - High (8.1). Network-reachable; requires only a standard authenticated user who is owner/admin of their own org (self-registration makes a user owner of their org, which holds `gitProviders:create`), so PR:L. High confidentiality (decrypted git OAuth client secret, GitHub App private key, webhook secret of another org) and high integrity (victim's provider reassigned to the attacker's org and overwritten). Precondition is knowing the victim's gitProviderId/githubId (random nanoids, not blind-enumerable); the published Dokploy IDOR advisories CVE-2026-72737 / CVE-2026-72876 carry the identical known-random-id precondition and were scored 9.6/9.9, so AC:L is consistent with vendor precedent. If the id is treated as a required secret (AC:H), ~6.8.

## Additional cross-org authorization gaps (same incomplete-org-scope root cause)

    [VERIFIED FROM SOURCE] network.networksToSync (network.ts:67, query) and network.import (network.ts:76, mutation):
      Both are bare `protectedProcedure` (NO withPermission). input.serverId -> getRemoteDocker(serverId) -> findServerById(serverId) with NO org check, then opens an SSH Dockerode connection to server.ipAddress using server.sshKey.privateKey. organizationId is used only for the local diff, never to authorize serverId.
      Impact: any member of any org makes the Dokploy host SSH into ANOTHER org's server using that org's stored SSH private key and run docker network ops (cross-tenant server info disclosure + unauthorized remote docker ops; import also writes rows). Enumerable serverId (nanoid). Novel.

    [SOURCE ANALYSIS -- re-verify before fix] project.duplicate (project.ts:840): protectedProcedure + checkProjectAccess(caller org) only; when duplicateInSameProject=false the inline org compare is skipped and client selectedServices[].id go to find<Service>ById(id) (no org) then re-created into the attacker's project -> clones another org's services incl. env build secrets + DB passwords + mounts/domains/ports.

    [SOURCE ANALYSIS -- re-verify before fix] service move (mariadb.ts:450, mongo/mysql/postgres/redis/libsql, application ~1002, compose ~776): source service is org-checked, but input.targetEnvironmentId is written unvalidated -> attacker relocates THEIR service into a victim org's environment (cross-org integrity write). Lower severity.

## Remediation
- git-provider update x4: load the provider and call `assertGitProviderAccess(ctx.session, provider)` before `updateGitProvider`, as the sibling one/getRepositories/getBranches/testConnection/remove/toggleShare do.
- network.networksToSync / network.import: add `withPermission` + resolve serverId through findServerById with an org-ownership assertion before getRemoteDocker.
- project.duplicate: org-check every selectedServices[].id against the caller's org before cloning.
- service move: validate input.targetEnvironmentId belongs to the caller's org before the UPDATE.
- Defense in depth: scope the underlying service UPDATE/SELECT (updateGitProvider etc.) by organizationId in the WHERE clause.

### Proof of concept

Preconditions: a Dokploy instance with two organizations. Attacker = owner/admin of org A. Victim = org B, which has configured a GitHub git provider (gitProviderId=GB, githubId=HB) carrying secrets (githubClientSecret/githubPrivateKey/githubWebhookSecret). Attacker learns GB/HB (ids appear in the victim's app URLs / API traffic).

1. Attacker (org A session) calls tRPC `github.update` with `{ gitProviderId: GB, githubId: HB, name: "x", githubAppName: "x", ... }` → `updateGitProvider` sets `gitProvider[GB].organizationId = <org A>` (no org check in WHERE).
2. The provider GB now belongs to org A. Attacker calls `github.one({ githubId: HB })` → `canViewGitProviderSecrets` passes (attacker is owner/admin of the now-owning org A) → response contains the DECRYPTED githubClientSecret, githubPrivateKey, githubWebhookSecret.

Result: cross-org disclosure of the victim's GitHub App credentials; the victim's provider is also moved out of org B (integration hijack/DoS).

LIVE-CONFIRMED on `dokploy/dokploy:v0.30.10` (two orgs on one instance; org B's provider seeded with marker secrets as victim setup; attacker used only its own self-registered org-A session):
- BEFORE - attacker `github.one` for the victim provider → HTTP 404 "Git provider not found" (cross-org read correctly denied).
- EXPLOIT - attacker `POST /api/trpc/github.update {"json":{"githubId":"HB-victim-gh-001","gitProviderId":"GB-victim-prov-01","name":"pwned-by-orgA","githubAppName":"pwned-by-orgA"}}` → HTTP 200 (no authz error); silently moves the provider into org A.
- AFTER - attacker `github.one` → HTTP 200 with githubClientSecret="VICTIM-CLIENT-SECRET", githubPrivateKey="VICTIM-PRIVATE-KEY", githubWebhookSecret="VICTIM-WEBHOOK-SECRET", and gitProvider.organizationId flipped to the attacker's org (DB-confirmed).

Full evidence: targets/dokploy/POC-GITPROVIDER-IDOR.md.

### Impact

Cross-organization theft of another organization's GitHub App credentials (decrypted OAuth client secret, GitHub App private key, webhook secret) and hijack/removal of its git integration, performed by any authenticated user who is merely owner/admin of their own self-registered organization. The companion network.networksToSync/import gaps additionally let any member drive the Dokploy host to SSH into another org's server using that org's stored private key. Affects multi-tenant Dokploy instances (any deployment hosting more than one organization).
repo.summary: Multiple cross-organization authorization gaps from incomplete org-scope coverage: git-provider update mutations reassign another org's provider and disclose its decrypted OAuth secrets/app key, plus network sync/import over another org's SSH key and service duplicate/move across orgs
